findings.impact: The code inspection shows a plausible fail-closed implementation, but the accepted security-sensitive ordering and packaging-failure behavior lacks the behavioral proof required by T025/T029. A later refactor could move runtime, authorization, durable creation or analysis ahead of identity rejection without this suite detecting the regression, and the current evidence overstates what was executed.
findings.remediation: Return to the T025 test-first owner. Add public/coordinator behavioral vectors for null, v1, malformed hash, wrong schema and identity-source exceptions, asserting Unavailable/HTTP 503 and zero runtime-resolution, fresh-authorization, initiation-store and preparation calls. Add executable source-level coverage for exactly-one resource, strict UTF-8, empty/schema-inconsistent rejection and exact decoded-text hash; introduce only the smallest accepted internal test seam if missing/duplicate/invalid-byte cases cannot otherwise be driven. Observe RED for any missing behavior, use the TDD implementer only where RED requires production correction, rerun surrounding T029/T030 tests, convergence and quality review, and correct the overstated verification evidence.

summary: REVISE with one Medium test-quality/evidence finding. The pinned production design and implementation are otherwise coherent: server-owned v2 identity, three authorization/currentness checks, deterministic exactly-two-Repository tuple replay, short PostgreSQL transactions, safe ambiguous-commit recovery, prepared-v2 result creation with legacy upgrade compatibility, CodeGraph 1.5/JDT-LS composition and prohibited-path guards all align with the accepted authorities. However T025/T029 explicitly require hostile identity and ordering vectors, while the actual tests exercise only the valid identity and unchanged legacy source; verification and convergence overstate that evidence. Return only to the T025 test-first owner, rerun invalidated convergence and quality review, and do not advance to T033 or T034-T045.
